Cut-over tooling: brain cutover …

The commands behind the saahil-docs → ~/brain/work move (runbook: brain-redesign box, plans/CUTOVER.md, steps C1, C2, C8, and the checks for C4/C5/C11). Every command is read-only unless --apply is given; every write keeps a backup.

C1  manifest ──► before.tsv ─┐
C4/C5  (the mv, by hand)     ├─► compare ──► same / changed-later / changed / missing / extra   (exit 1: missing or changed)
    manifest ──► after.tsv ──┘
C2  laptop.tsv + devbox.tsv ──► reconcile ──► report.md   (--apply --machine M: rename M's losing copies aside)
C8  rewrite-paths <work/box> --from OLD… --to NEW          (dry run: per-file counts; --apply: backup + atomic replace)
C11 find-names <roots…>                                     (names, text mentions and link targets still left)

Manifest (manifest <root> --out F)

One TSV row per entry, in filepath.WalkDir order, after a # header:

column value
path relative to the root, /-separated; Go-quoted when it holds a control char or \, is -, or starts with #/"
size bytes (- for a directory)
mtime RFC 3339 UTC, nanoseconds
sha256 regular files ≤ 2 MB not under a --skip-hash-under glob; else - (compare then uses size + mtime)
type file · dir · symlink · other
target the symlink's target (never followed), else -

A symlinked root (the compat link after the swap) is resolved; symlinked directories inside are rows, never walked. Hashing runs on ≤ 8 workers with ≤ 32 rows in flight, so memory does not grow with the tree. Files that vanish mid-walk are counted, not listed. The output is written as F.partial and renamed at the end; an existing F, or an F inside the root, is refused.

compare and reconcile merge-join two manifests in that order (component-wise: a/x before a-c) and refuse an out-of-order manifest. A move keeps sizes, hashes and mtimes, so any difference is either a later edit (newer mtime, --allow-newer lists it as changed-later) or a failure.

Reconcile (reconcile <laptop.tsv> <devbox.tsv> --out R.md)

Text files hashed on both sides with different content: the newer mtime wins (a tie goes to the devbox, which holds the originals). The loser's plan is <file>.conflict-<loser machine>-<loser mtime, 20060102T150405Z>, derived from the manifests only, so both machines compute the same plan. --apply --machine M --root DIR renames M's losing copies aside, only when the file still has its manifest sha and the conflict name is free; the winner arrives by the normal sync. Unhashed, binary and file-vs-directory differences are listed, not resolved.

Rewrite (rewrite-paths <root> --from P… --to P)

Replaces every old prefix (* = one path component, e.g. a worktree slug; longest prefix first) in text files ≤ 10 MB and in symlink targets. Never touched: binaries (NUL in the first 8 KB, or a known binary extension), .env* files (never even opened), and history — .git/, log/, .archive/, transcripts/, <uuid>.jsonl session transcripts, manifest*.{tsv,csv,json,jsonl,txt}. Venv files are reported by role (venv:pyvenv.cfg, venv:activate, venv:script for both #!<venv>/bin/python and pip's long-path '''exec' form, venv:symlink); a rewrite that would make a #! line longer than 127 bytes is refused.

--apply (backup dir default ~/brain/.archive/cutover/rewrite-<UTC>/, must be outside the root and fresh):

  1. copy the original to <backup>/files/<path> with its mode and mtime;
  2. write the new bytes to a temp file beside it, keep the mode, fsync;
  3. rename over the original only if its size and mtime are unchanged since it was read (a live writer wins; the file is reported and left alone). The new file's mtime is now.
  4. append path kind occurrences mtime_before sha256_before sha256_after target_before target_after to <backup>/manifest.tsv.

Undo a file: copy <backup>/files/<path> back. Undo a link: ln -sfn <target_before> <path>.

Find (find-names <root…>)

Lists every non-history entry named saahil-docs (name:dir|file|symlink), every text file containing it (text, with a count) and every symlink whose target contains it (link-target), then counts by kind and file category. History and .env* are excluded as above.
